findings.description: AWS access key and secret key are hardcoded in plaintext within the instance user_data script, which is stored in the instance metadata and Terraform state, exposing long-lived credentials to anyone with access to either.
The EBS volume does not set encrypted = true, meaning data at rest on this volume is unencrypted and vulnerable to exposure if the underlying storage is compromised.
The EBS snapshot inherits the unencrypted state of its source volume, resulting in unencrypted data at rest that could be exposed if the snapshot is shared or accessed improperly.
The security group allows inbound SSH (port 22) from 0.0.0.0/0, exposing the instance to brute-force and unauthorized access attempts from anywhere on the internet.
The security group allows inbound HTTP (port 80) traffic from 0.0.0.0/0 with no additional protections, increasing the attack surface for the web service.

findings.issue_category: missing encryption and public access controls
findings.description: The S3 bucket used for VPC flow logs has no server-side encryption configuration and no public access block or bucket policy restricting access, potentially exposing sensitive network flow log data.
The subnet has map_public_ip_on_launch set to true, causing instances launched here to automatically receive public IP addresses, increasing exposure to the internet.
The subnet has map_public_ip_on_launch set to true, causing instances launched here to automatically receive public IP addresses, increasing exposure to the internet.
